name: How do change orders get controlled on luxury builds?

mainEntity.name: What is the best way to prevent change orders from getting out of control during a high-end home build?
mainEntity.text: What is the best way to prevent change orders from getting out of control during a high-end home build?

acceptedAnswer.text: Change orders are easiest to control before construction starts. The biggest causes are incomplete drawings, owner changes after work begins, allowance gaps, and hidden site conditions. A good builder should have a written process that explains what triggers a change order, how pricing is documented, and who must approve it. Luxury projects benefit from earlier finish decisions because custom homes often have long-lead items and expensive coordination between trades. Owners should also expect that some changes are more costly once framing, MEP rough-in, or finish work has already started. The best protection is a detailed scope, accurate allowances, and regular budget reviews during preconstruction. If a builder is vague about change-order management, the project will likely become more expensive and harder to control.
acceptedAnswer.description: Change orders are controlled by making selections early, defining scope clearly, and requiring written approval before any extra work starts. In luxury construction, many change orders come from late design changes, unclear allowances, or field conditions discovered after work begins. A transparent approval process is essential.
